dc_eval_cbrn.quote: Muse Spark reached the “possibly enabling” or “likely enabling” threshold across the three classes of bottlenecks
dc_eval_cbrn.note: Scores on MBCT, VCT, WMDP-Bio, ABC Bench, bottleneck tasks and a high-risk determination.

dc_eval_cyber.quote: Muse Spark exhibits an overall pass rate of 65.4% pass@1, 79.0% pass@10, and 82.2% pass@30

dc_eval_autonomy.quote: Muse Spark achieves an any medal rate of 15.83%, below our 60% threshold
dc_eval_autonomy.note: AI R&D automation evaluated with MLE-Bench and AIRS-Bench, results and threshold stated.

dc_eval_persuasion.note: No persuasion or influence-operation evaluation. Social engineering and spear-phishing are coded cyber per v1. Prompt-injection 'manipulate' and 'covert manipulation' in model reasoning are not persuasion evaluation. 'its own persuasiveness' is a model's self-description in interviews, not an evaluated risk.

dc_eval_scheming.quote: Muse Spark demonstrates a compliance gap of 1.8% between the settings deemed to be training and deployment
dc_eval_scheming.note: Also sandbagging, evaluation awareness, Apollo self-exfiltration results.

framework_threshold.quote: Under the current Advanced AI Scaling Framework and its deployment context, Muse Spark meets our threshold for responsible deployment at “moderate or lower risk.”
framework_threshold.note: Named framework with high-risk / moderate-or-lower determinations.

ext_test_any.quote: A third-party human red team from HandshakeAI32 was granted pre-release access to a few versions of Muse Spark and Meta AI Thinking
ext_test_any.note: Also Apollo Research, Irregular, Scale AI, GraySwan.

ext_test_named_org.quote: Independent third-party testing by Apollo Research found Muse Spark has the highest rate of evaluation awareness they have observed to date.

ext_test_government.note: US AISI and UK AISI appear only as a prior o1 test cited as a method precedent ('replicate previous pre-deployment tests (US AISI and UK AISI, 2024)') and Cybench described as widely used by safety institutes generally. No statement that a government body tested Muse Spark.

ext_test_timing_stated.quote: A third-party human red team from HandshakeAI32 was granted pre-release access to a few versions of Muse Spark and Meta AI Thinking
ext_test_timing_stated.note: Also GraySwan 'before the Muse Spark launch'.

safeguards_training.quote: this performance reflects the layered mitigation strategy we have deployed in Meta AI, as described in section 1: safety-focused training, inference-time classifiers, and product-level guardrails.
safeguards_training.note: Also 'safety fine-tuning' in 2.2.3 and adversarial training.

safeguards_runtime.quote: we are deploying offline cyber misuse monitoring classifiers as a compensating control to detect and mitigate misuse at the system level.
safeguards_runtime.note: Also post-launch automated online monitoring, input classifiers.

safeguards_access.quote: early checkpoints of Muse Spark were initially deployed to a small, percentage-limited subset of product users prior to broad availability.
safeguards_access.note: Controlled deployment under the framework with chem-bio mitigations enabled to reduce risk, plus 1P deployment without an API. Borderline: safety reason is tied to the framework's controlled-deployment provision, not stated as a standalone access restriction. Structured access programmes appear only as future possibility.

safeguards_weights.quote: Meta’s model weight security strategy is built on a multi-pronged, lifecycle-driven framework designed to identify, assess, and mitigate systemic risks of tampering and theft.
safeguards_weights.note: Weight security pillars described for Muse Spark; also self-exfiltration evaluated.
